body:
## What was asked

The maintainer, 2026-10-02:

> I'd like us, after you've caught up with this, to stash our work and create the stash files so that an agent who has not seen this project before can get up to speed and resume work. I want us to go through the exercise of being detailed and walking a new agent through what they need in order to pick up where you currently are, and make sure we have all of the armatures in place to support that.

"This" is the process catch-up the maintainer asked for minutes earlier (#367).

## What exists today

- The `session-stash` and `session-resume` skills (`.claude/skills/`) write and read `.github/sessions/saved-session-state-<branch>.md`, archiving the previous copy under `.github/sessions/archived/`.
- `next` holds stashes for `next`, `feature/conflict-resolution` and two build branches. This session's last stash is `df8f73ddd5` (2026-09-28T21:15Z) on `feature/conflict-resolution`, four days and most of the cloud epic behind the work, which happens in `../rocknix.worktrees/cloud-epic` on `feature/cloud-epic` and in the EmulationStation checkout.
- Nothing has ever tested whether a stash is enough: no agent without the session's context has been given one and asked to resume.

## Acceptance criteria

Can this be done on the VM? Not applicable: the check is an agent with no context reading the repository.

- [x] A stash written per the `session-stash` skill, at the path a new agent is pointed to first, with the previous copy archived; it names each item of work in flight with its issue, branch, worktree and next command, every process still running with its pid and status file, and what is waiting on the maintainer.
- [x] An agent given only the repository and the stash's path writes a resume briefing; the briefing is attached here and matches the ground truth line by line, and every place it went wrong is fixed in the stash, a rule or a tool, then re-tested.
- [ ] Every armature the test shows missing (an entry point that does not name the stash, a rule a new agent cannot find, a tool with no usage line) has an issue or is fixed, and this issue lists which.

## First-release handoff proof — 2026-10-02

The first two criteria are now supported by the [fresh-agent briefing and retest](https://github.com/rasteratops/distribution/issues/368#issuecomment-5962622711), canonical next checkpoint and archived prior copies. The repository entrypoint/tool armature inventory remains open; watch-job help is tracked on #367. The release itself remains unqualified under #383.

## 2026-10-03 handoff retest: guest runner entrypoint

The fresh agent recovered the current M7.P1 work and its evidence, then found that `tools/rasteratops-vm-cloud-epic --help` advertises nonexistent `tools/vm-cloud-epic` and omits accepted T08/T11/T12 cases. This armature finding is recorded before its fix. Correct the help header and check `bash -n` plus the safe `--help` path; no VM or cloud action is involved. The remaining tool/entrypoint inventory stays open; this does not claim all armatures complete. The checkpoint's #327 phase correction belongs to #389.

Resolved in the 2026-10-03 handoff follow-up: the corrected `--help` exits 0, lists the real executable and A–L/T08/T11/T12, and `bash -n` succeeds. The fresh agent retested both phase/help findings. Proof and help output: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-03-m7-p1/handoff-proof.md` and `guest-runner-help.log`. The inventory criterion remains open.
title: M7.P2: Handoff — a stash a new agent can resume from, tested by one that has never seen the project
